sent_to_model:
Good morning. Our congregation bought a Lindqvist Optics PT-20 camera last winter to replace the webcam we had been livestreaming worship with since 2020, and the supplier, Chancel AV, has emailed twice asking for a review on their product page. I'd like to give them an honest one. Other small churches read those reviews before spending money they don't have, so it should be specific about setup, picture quality and what it did and didn't fix for us. I'm not an engineer and won't pretend to be one, but I've learned more about this thing than I expected to. Their form has a star box, but please state our rating in the text itself as well, since people skim.

- paid $2,140 from Chancel AV in February 2026, wall mount was another $95
- 20x optical zoom, 1080p60, NDI HX and plain HDMI out, PoE so one cable up to the balcony
- runs into OBS on the old office PC, streams to our YouTube channel, 30-60 viewers most Sundays
- 9 presets stored - altar, pulpit, lectern, font, choir loft, piano, wide, two for the chancel steps
- nave is 92 feet long, camera mounted on the balcony rail at the back
- first Sunday the presets drifted a few degrees by the sermon; firmware update 2.4 in March fixed it
- Easter Vigil candlelight service in April, the first 'Christ the Lord Is Risen Today' with only candles; picture got grainy but stayed usable, old webcam showed nothing but dots
- Delores (82, homebound) called to say she could finally read the hymn numbers on the board
- Erik, our 16-year-old acolyte, runs it from the free web app on a tablet; learned it in one afternoon
- autofocus hunts when someone walks between camera and pulpit, so we lock focus on presets
- manual is thin and badly translated; Chancel AV tech support (Marcy) was excellent on the phone
- audio is not the camera's job and it did nothing for our sound problem, people should know that
- 4 stars; would buy again, but a congregation under 100 might do fine with something cheaper
- useful to another small parish deciding whether it is worth the money
- plain about the limits, no salesmanship

(About me: Lutheran pastor, 61, Minneapolis, Minnesota. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: States a four-star rating in the review text.
Describes setup and control using the supplied experience.
Explains picture quality, the preset fix and autofocus limitations.
Makes clear the camera did not fix the sound problem.
Helps another small parish judge whether the camera is worth the cost.
